for_you_if: you enjoy relaxing open-world driving experiences
you want a sprawling recreation of North American highways

citations.review_text: It claims Steam Deck verified, but it's uncontrollable. The control schemes are all outdated, the official ones lack basic menu support. I was never even able to get into a truck to try driving because every single input scheme I tried was utterly broken.
Terrible controls. It's impossible to set up a controller. I don't understand how they made it more difficult to set up a controller than it is to solve quantum physics equations.

my entire 26 minutes was trying to get it to work with my controller
wish id tried when it was still within the timeframe required for a refund >.<
some may like this game. I will come back and try again when it has better controller support.

How come when i press reset binds i have it deletes all the original controller keys too so i have to spend a lot of timne rebinding everything, Do NOT PLAY WITHOUT STEERING WHEEL And shifter as it sucks on controller I am willing to reinstall to see if that helps but im not sure yet

claims.claim: Reviewers report that convoy mode experiences matchmaking or connectivity issues when players have a DLC mismatch.

citations.review_text: Convoy mode doesn't work if you have DLC mismatch. If someone with no DLC hosts then someone with DLC should still be able to do join. But this jank game doesn't work.

I built a sim rig where I thought I would spend most of my time racing. But somehow, I spend more time in this game than actual racing games. The simple pleasure of driving and seeing the world while listening to Truckers FM while in a convoy with friends is total choice. Is it the most optimized game, not by a long shot. The networking could use a ton of work, but even in the state it is in I still recommend it.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the driving is a bit stiff with wasd, though it works good enough.

citation.review_text:
I like Ets 2 more. Its not only where i live, i think the countries are far more diverse than the one very big country with a lot of different states.. opinions can differ. I drive in the states using kg and km/h. the road signs are weird, but I am getting used to calculating what a "65" sign for instance really means ;)
But its one big plus is the huge amount of new map it offers. After driving through most of europe. So this is why I am here. aand there are new trucks as well, but they are either weird looking or have huge turn radius or both. ^^
But some of them are kind of beautiful, I have to admit: the long nose is a unique selling point you dont get in europe. But be ready to suffer. (turn radius)

A nice extra is turning right on red is allowed. If you are at a red traffic light in pole position: put your blinkers on, wait for the traffic to pass and stay in your lane - then you can drive while the lights are red! weird, right? yes: only right turns!

If you are new to this: You dont HAVE to be one of those mil-sim truckers with steering-wheels and everything. I drive this not for the immersion of sitting in a truck. I am very glad I am not in one actually. ^^ so mouse and keyboard here. I still like it, although the driving is a bit stiff with wasd, I have to admit. But it works for me good enough.

btw: If you want to experience driving a few dozen tons of steel down the road at top speed with your favourite music blasting your ears and sipping a beer or 2? THIS is the ONLY place you can do that. ;)

single_points.text: One reviewer states that it is hard to see which achievements can be completed without owning the DLC because of the over 100+ achievements shown for downloadable content.

citation.review_text:
The game itself is pretty good and I like it, but I do have a few complaints, though they aren't major despite this being a 10 year old game. 

I do really like the mechanics of this game and think it's pretty realistic, and the effort put into this is amazing, but i want to see what achievements I'm able to get without only seeing the ones available for me to do without seeing over 100+ achievements for DLCs, it really makes it hard to see which I'm able to get, and which i cant without having to look at each and everyone. 

Another thing I have a small complaint about is how sensitive the cones are in the driving academy, I'll barely if not, just scrap by one, and it'll immediately mark it as wrong, with NO checkpoints, i get the cones, as they could be sensitive for this being 10 years old, but no checkpoints on long chapter episodes where I'll have to do at least 5 minutes of work all over because of a small mess-up? I feel like maybe halfway the chapters should have checkpoints, maybe not easy ones, but for sure on the harder ones where it's easier to mess up, just don't add them on the final exams either. 

Besides these complaints, this game is overall pretty good, and i do enjoy playing this! These are just things I've struggled and got frustrated with, but overall, good game.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Regular updates disrupt existing modifications, necessitating troubleshooting to find incompatible files.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that frequent game updates break existing modifications, requiring time-consuming troubleshooting to identify incompatible files.

citations.review_text:
Great Sim, but a nightmare if you enjoy mods.
I've spent over 400 hrs playing this since its release and have nearly every DLC. I really do enjoy almost every aspect of this sim, the atmosphere, the physics, it's very relaxing and even more fun with friends. 

HOWEVER,
The constant updates can be VERY infuriating for modders. Myself, I use an average of 60 mods, ranging from trucks that aren't in the game, to engines with more power, and overall quality of life fixes and improvements. Everytime I want to play the game now there has recently been ANOTHER update, thus requiring me to sort through EVERY SINGLE MOD until I find the one that crashed my game, usually taking me an average of 1.5 hrs or more. It is to the point now that I just don't want to do it anymore. 

Great Game/Sim without mods, but 10/10 with mods. But now I might just lay it to rest for good.

I use to love this game so much. Now my controls messed up from all these updates. If you're going to do so many updates why not do a big one instead. 
Small updates get annoying when it breaks mods. but other then that really good game wish the cops actually pulled you over that would be amazing.

Unfortunately, I have to leave a negative review.
ATS isn't a bad game, but it’s a bit of a joke.

Even after more than 10 years of development, it is, in reality, still in an "early access" state.
I could overlook the fact that—even after a decade—you still can't get out of your truck, and many so on ...
Here you can drive through various states and climate zones, but only in the summer. ONLY in the summer.
The inability to include seasons in the game is disgraceful.

And before you bring up the argument that I can just add seasons via mods—let me stop you right there: that’s an invalid argument.
Since the game is effectively still in early access, updates are released very frequently.
This means that mods often become outdated almost immediately, frequently ending up incompatible with the new version.

If the mod creator is active, you might be back up and running in a few days.
If they aren't, it takes longer—sometimes much longer. 
You’re often left with a choice: keep waiting ... and waiting (indefinitely, perhaps), or uninstall the mod just so you can play. In the summer!

The game, along with all its DLCs (most of which I own), costs around $250! And for that price, you don't get spring, autumn, or winter—no snow, no tire chains, no slippery roads. Just summer.
IT’S A DISGRACE!
So, for $250, you get a "realistic" driving experience in Montana—without any snow—and soon, presumably, in Canada—also without any snow.
This has to be a joke. It’s just ...

I absolutely cannot fathom how SCS can pass this off as a "finished game," and call it a "simulator," and still garner so many positive reviews.
Just think about this:
Imagine a Flight Simulator where you can only fly under clear skies - stupid, right?
Imagine playing *Train Sim World*—but only in the summer stupid, right?
Or *GTA*, but only during the day :)) — one endless day.
Well, here you have one endless summer ;)
(I don’t think any *GTA* game ever cost $250, and even *GTA VI* won’t cost that much) 

SCS is…

single_points.text: One reviewer says there needs to be universal settings for convoys, flexibility to chain jobs together, and some help in the vehicle/trailer configuration in-game.

citation.review_text: While there's a couple things I'd definitely tweak I enjoy the game very much.  There needs to be some universal settings for convoys, flexibility to "chain' jobs together, and updates need to be less of a enterprise that breaks things each time.  Some help in the vehicle/trailer configuration in-game would be great.  Also some of the locations need to more relevant; sending a tanker to a big box store to pick up oil doesn't make much sense.  More options to paint equipment would be fun.

single_points.text: One reviewer says once you go past a certain number of mods, the game can start crashing.

citation.review_text:
My only real issue is stability with mods: once you go past a certain number of them, the game can start crashing, which ruins the fun.

Multiplayer and convoys could also use some work. Lobbies are limited to 8 players, and everyone needs the same mods in the same load order. Optional mods effectively do nothing.

Overall, a solid game that’s held back a bit by mod stability and limited convoy options.
